Rothfusz regression with NWS low/high-humidity adjustments. Bands: 80–90 caution · 91–103 extreme caution · 104–124 danger · 125+ extreme danger.

📖 How to use

  1. Enter the air temperature (°F or °C).
  2. Enter the relative humidity (%).
  3. Read the heat index and its danger-level band.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What is the heat index formula?

The Rothfusz regression, published by the US National Weather Service, combines air temperature (°F) and relative humidity (%) into one 'feels like' number. Low-humidity (≤13%) and high-humidity (>85%) adjustments from the NWS are applied.

What are the heat danger levels?

80–90°F caution, 91–103°F extreme caution, 104–124°F danger, 125°F+ extreme danger. The tool labels your result automatically.

Does shade change the heat index?

Shade can make it feel up to 15°F cooler, while full sun can add up to 15°F to the heat index value.
